caveat: Non-Flock readers come only from volunteer mapping in OpenStreetMap, which is incomplete: OSM had mapped 65.3% of Flock's in-service readers in the city (73.9% north of Madison Street, 57.1% south), so non-Flock readers are likely undercounted, more so on the South Side. Flock's inventory is complete but dates from December 2025.

wards.value: a Chicago ward (2023 map): its area, 2020 population, the plate readers inside it, and how far its residents live from the nearest one

community_areas.value: a Chicago community area: its area, 2020 population, the plate readers inside it, and how far its residents live from the nearest one

tracts.value: a 2020 Cook County census tract at least 1% inside Chicago: its area, 2020 population, the plate readers inside it, and how far its residents live from the nearest one

alpr_per_sqkm.keywords: license plate reader readers lpr alpr flock camera cameras surveillance police tracking privacy
alpr_per_sqkm.label: Plate Reader Density
alpr_per_sqkm.methodology: License-plate readers of every vendor from OpenStreetMap (surveillance:type=ALPR; © OpenStreetMap contributors), merged with Flock Safety's in-service plate readers from the December 2025 device inventory behind Proton's Flock camera map; an OSM reader within 50 m of a Flock device is treated as that device. Readers counted per area and divided by its land area. Computed directly for wards and community areas; other boundaries take the 2020 census tracts that overlap them. Fewer readers is scored as better here, a privacy reading; others count the same cameras as a public-safety investment, so the measure is unweighted by default.
